source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_D::U24: Distinguish actionable-claim assignment from secured-debt transfer

payload.title: Identify the claim and protect the payment trail
payload.core_explanation_md:
The described actionable-claim definition concerns the qualifying unsecured debt or beneficial movable-property interest outside possession, and excludes the specified mortgage, hypothecation or pledge-secured debts. Do not treat every banking receivable as identical merely because it involves money.

The assignment route requires the prescribed signed written instrument. Notice to the debtor is not the sole event creating the transfer, but lack of notice can affect the treatment of payments or dealings before the debtor knows of it. The transferee has the described ability to sue in their own name, subject to the applicable law. Keep the instrument, claim identification, notice and payment history together; assignment is not proved by an internal spreadsheet entry.

self_check.prompt_text: Does absence of debtor notice automatically mean no assignment could occur?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Transfer formalities and debtor-protection consequences differ.

payload.stem_md: A portfolio includes debts secured by pledge, and a note assumes every debt is an actionable claim under the stated definition. What is missing?

options.text_md: The exclusion for the specified secured debts
options.explanation_md: The definition is not every receivable.

options.text_md: A rule that money claims cannot be transferred
options.explanation_md: The source recognises a transfer route for qualifying claims; the question concerns the definition exclusions.
It does not classify the claim.

options.explanation_md: Visual formatting does not establish the signed assignment instrument or the legal transfer formalities.
